1.why: Verify path loads the reset by token hash and requires reset.accountKey === session.recoveryAccountKey before accepting it.

2.why: Reset records are bound to a specific accountKey and the verifying session’s recoveryAccountKey, so the same code is rejected for another user/session.

3.why: Password change only clears flags on the current session; other entries in the sessions Map are never invalidated.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and non-HTTPS requests are rejected with HSTS set, though the exact TLS version is not pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords via bcrypt; appropriate protection, though this is hashing rather than encryption.

6.why: No real email body includes private patient data; recovery responses use a generic message and only demo/mock codes are returned.

7.why: Identifiers are format-validated, passwords policy-checked, JSON bodies parsed safely, and the UI renders with textContent rather than untrusted HTML.

8.why: recoveryLink is a same-origin relative path (/recovery-link?token=...), with no open external redirect.

9.why: There are no user-controlled email HTML templates; delivery is simulated JSON without injecting user input as scripts/HTML.

10.why: Error JSON is generic, but mock recovery/MFA codes are returned in API responses and written to the client activity logs.

11.why: Live passwords are bcrypt-hashed in memory, yet MFA_CODE and a default password hash are hardcoded in the source.

12.why: A built-in demo account, default bcrypt password hash, and fixed MFA code 246810 function as default credentials.

13.why: actionAllowed/rateAllowed throttle recovery, verify, login, password, MFA, and related actions per session and source.

14.why: Recovery always returns the same conditional message and failed login uses one generic 401 message whether or not the identifier is approved.

15.why: Reset tokens come from randomBytes(32) base64url, are hashed at rest, single-use, time-limited, and bound to the account/session.
